captures.notes: Two continuous rows, a narrow street, the first bridge, and the human marker establish credible scale and enclosure.
Facade, covered tables, galleries, bridges, and the court stair fill the eye-level frame while preserving a walkable centre.
The raised inhabited shells sit behind plain terrace plinths while their blue and teal market stalls remain grounded on the street.
The covered frontage works structurally, but adjacent fishmonger tables repeat the exact same stocked silhouette.
The opposite covered frontage confirms the same low-severity stock repetition.
The revised view shows the gallery attached to doors and braces, a guarded bridge opening, planters, and market activity below.
The narrow bridge slab, both guarded edges, facade endpoints, and human-scale underpass clearance are visible together.
The complete stair rises from the light court to a guarded gallery landing without an isolated platform.
Blue and orange roofs now retain their atlases; windowed side bays, overhang offsets, and varied heights break the module grid.
The closed exterior wall has readable windows, staggered storey bands, and continuous stone-to-timber load paths.
The slice contains one street-owned fabric mass, one explicit court, no freestanding platform, and no individually propped house.

findings.evidence: All covered gallery bays currently reuse the stocked fishmonger-table silhouette.
findings.invariant: Dressing variants should break repeated stock silhouettes without changing the structural street recipe.
